title: (No AI) Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial
author: Adi Robertson
content:
![CEO of Meta Platforms Mark Zuckerberg (R) looks on as U.S. President Donald Trump holds a press briefing with AI executives following a meeting on artificial intelligence, outside the West Wing of the White House on September 29, 2026 in Washington, DC.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/gettyimages-2297777001.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

President Donald Trump has a knack for turning words against his enemies. His first successful presidential run was built on monikers like "Little Marco" and "Crooked Hillary"; he changed "fake news" from [a phrase](http://journalism.org/2016/12/15/many-americans-believe-fake-news-is-sowing-confusion/) describing scammy media outlets to a derogatory term for the press at large. Over the past few weeks, he's clearly decided he can work the same magic to promote artificial intelligence - branding a technology he wants to accelerate "super", while turning "artificial" into his latest go-to pejorative and [declaring resisters](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117406176604364910) "THE ENEMY." Some of the biggest names in AI are going along with him. But he's picked a tough linguistic batt …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/policy/1008677/trump-super-intelligence-ai-rebranding)

title: (No AI) Instinct was the buzziest AI agent around — can it survive Muse?
author: Allison Johnson
content:
![Photo of a phone on a table showing Instinct AI texts.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/DSC04328_processed_1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Instinct’s agent is always just a text away.

Before there were [cute little guys](https://www.theverge.com/column/999999/optimizer-meta-muse-ai-cute), there was Instinct.

In August, the startup got its AI agent to market with an unusual playbook: invite-only, no marketing, and barely so much as a website. And yet, Instinct quickly became the buzziest thing in AI, [garnering praise](https://www.wired.com/story/i-finally-found-an-ai-agent-worth-the-risk/) for its straightforward, text message-based interface and its ability to handle chores like [booking DMV appointments](https://x.com/pitdesi/status/2090579987778937159?lang=en) and [sending follow-up emails](https://x.com/srcasm/status/2091211911920542200).

Then Muse arrived, followed not long after by Dots. The same products, more or less, from two far more powerful companies.

With Big Tech players suddenly in the mix, it was looking dubious that the startup's buzzy launch could keep …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1008254/instinct-agent-ai-hands-on-muse-dots)
